value.content: A computational workflow applying Logical Data Analysis (LDA) to investigate destruction patterns among ancient Egyptian objects from the Cachette de Karnak. The workflow formalises observed destruction features as a binary context over 333 objects and uses the RAP (Rules and Patterns) algorithm, implemented in **OSCAR** via **Jupyter Notebook**, to extract a minimal implication basis from the data. The derived logical rules are evaluated for statistical and scientific relevance, testing whether damage distributions encode systematic, intentional destruction practice.\N\N### Main steps\N\N**Extract objects** — extract 333 relevant objects from the Cachette de Karnak database.\N\N**Define properties** — define discriminating properties for the subset.\N\N**Encode objects** — encode each object as a binary string per property.\N\N**Compute rules** — compute the Gröbner basis of the boolean ring to extract logical rules.\N\N**Interpret results** — evaluate the statistical and scientific relevance of the derived implications.
